A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same B3 research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original B3/B3++ experiments on MMEB and caption retrieval, alongside component ablations and batch-size analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original text-only sentence-similarity results, a CLIP-teacher experiment and further data and hyperparameter analyses.

M1.justification: The teacher-ranking, METIS batch construction, optional unified hard-negative sampling and prompting procedures are retained. Section 3.1.1 newly specifies retaining bidirectional edges when constructing the undirected graph. This supplies a previously unspecified implementation detail; the PDFs do not establish an actual change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Section 4.7 extends evaluation beyond the retained multimodal benchmarks to text-only learning: training on NLI data and evaluating sentence similarity on STS12–16, STS-B and SICK-R. This adds a distinct training domain and evaluation task.

E2.justification: Table 6 introduces evaluated SimCSE comparators with and without annotated hard negatives. Table 5 also brings the existing Random Batches control into the teacher-strength comparison. Comparator membership in the original main benchmark, caption-retrieval and GBM comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce substantial additional protocols: 300M RoBERTa-Large models trained on 275K NLI examples at batch size 512, with and without one annotated hard negative; a CLIP(400M) teacher setting; and VQA-only and retrieval-only sensitivity experiments at batch size 32. The previously reported main MMEB settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 extends teacher-strength analysis to a substantially weaker CLIP teacher. Appendix G adds target-length analyses, VQA-specific exclusion-threshold tests and retrieval-specific candidate-window sweeps, strengthening investigation of false negatives and parameter sensitivity. Table 11 largely tabulates the existing Figure 3 analysis rather than introducing an entirely new robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The unchanged assertion that results are statistically meaningful does not constitute added uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original benchmark scores in Tables 1–3 and all plotted results remain unchanged. New Table 5 reports 67.30 average accuracy with a CLIP teacher, versus 67.58 with VLM2Vec(2B) under matching batch and cluster sizes. Table 6 adds B3/SimCSE averages of 81.62/80.86 without annotated hard negatives and 84.24/83.57 with them, although B3 scores lower on SICK-R. Appendix G adds target-length and sensitivity results.

T1.justification: The loss definitions, Theorems 1–2, optimization expression, Appendix E proof and Appendix F argument about K are retained. Appendix H supplies conceptual clustering justification without adding a formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add explicit claims of cross-domain generalization and effectiveness with considerably weaker teachers. The central batch-mining contribution, MMEB performance margins and small-batch efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism explanations: teachers need identify only some strong negatives; stronger teachers may offer little benefit once those negatives suffice; short VQA answers motivate greater false-negative exclusion; and larger batches reduce parameter sensitivity. Appendix H adds reasons for selecting METIS over alternative clustering approaches. The stated compute limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents mutual-edge graph construction and discloses that p was tuned at smaller batch sizes and reused for larger batches. It also supplies model, dataset-size, batch-size and hard-negative details for the new text-only experiments. Existing LoRA settings, hardware, runtime disclosures and repository address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Morris and Rush's Contextual Document Embeddings and positions its clustering approach as limited to text-only benchmarks and smaller models. The previous cited works and broader research positioning are retained; subsequent reference renumbering is not substantive.

P1.justification: v2 formats the contributions as bullets, introduces numbered ablation subsections, adds a generalization subsection and two explanatory appendices, and moves the prompts appendix from G to I. Most existing prose and the main narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: The teacher comparison is separated from Table 4 into an expanded Table 5. New Table 6 presents sentence-similarity results, and Tables 7–12 present data characteristics and parameter analyses. Main-table captions move above their tables, while the original prompt table becomes Table 13. All five figure graphics are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The weaker-teacher and text-only experiments strengthen evidence for B3's applicability, while Appendix G and the explicit graph-construction detail improve understanding and reproducibility. These provide useful additional validation beyond v1. However, the new STS results lack an explicitly identified metric and uncertainty estimates, limiting the strength and reproducibility of that extension. Overall, the gains support a limited net improvement.
